thread:
lee: Heads up — last night ~00:12 UTC we saw tenant=acme hit the full fallback chain on /v1/generate. It matched the route but then got routed down to lowcost-quant after two CB trips. Latency spiked and quality dipped. attaching quick summary and logs below.

mira: Do we have a CB timeline? were these latency CBs or error-rate?

sam: Error vs latency: from the traces it looks like latency-driven CB. backend p95 crossed 500ms -> cb opened on standard lane, then premium tried to absorb but was at capacity.

ops-bot: [ALERT] tenant-acme fallback_count=14 in 5m window, primary_lane_saturation=92%, standard_lane_cb_open=true

lee: Key questions: 1) route matching precedence — we want header-level overrides from the gateway to stick (X-Tenant-Priority), 2) allow a soft quota bump for a short grace window before forcing quantized fallback, 3) CB thresholds might be too aggressive for our sequence lengths.

mira: Agreed. Proposal: change ordering so that route-level header affinity is evaluated before global capacity-based spillback. Also add a 30s grace quota override for tenants hitting sudden spike if they've got active rollout tags. Pseudoconfig: 

```yaml
routes:
  - name: generate-v1
    match:
      path: /v1/generate
      headers:
        X-Tenant-Priority: high|normal|low
    precedence: header
    fallback_chain:
      - lane: premium
        cb: {type: latency, threshold_ms: 400, window_s: 30}
      - lane: standard
        cb: {type: latency, threshold_ms: 600, window_s: 30}
      - lane: lowcost-quant
        cb: {type: latency, threshold_ms: 1200, window_s: 60}
    grace_quota_on_spike: 30s
```

sam: I like the idea. Two caveats: (a) grace_quota needs clear telemetry so we don't mask actual capacity problems, (b) we should prefer backup models that are same-architecture quantized variants before switching to smaller-context models — quality cliff is lower that way.

lee: Good call on same-arch quantized first. Also we should add a fallback metric: fallback_step{tenant,route,step} and fallback_latency_impact{tenant}. Need these surfaced in console and paired with traces so PMs can triage quality regressions.

mira: For CB tuning — suggestion: make threshold adaptive based on recent seq_len distribution. If seq_len_p95 < 128 then bump thresholds by 1.5x, else keep defaults. That avoids opening CB on workloads with naturally higher per-token time.

sam: That will help. Implementation note: don't bake this into route YAML initially — expose as feature flag + canary in console -> metric rollout.

deploy-bot: Starting canary: route-config v2026-03-17-09: header-precedence + grace-quota flag -> 5% traffic to canary cluster.

ops-bot: Canary observed: fallback_count down 42% for canary tenants in first 10m, but premium_lane CPU rose 8% (within SLA). Logging suggests most avoided lowcost-quant.

lee: Excellent. Next actions: 1) Mira to land header-precedence + grace_quota feature flag (small PR w/ tests), 2) Sam to add fallback_step + fallback_latency_impact metrics + console chart, 3) Ops to monitor canary for 2h then promote if stable.

mira: I'll open PR now, will add e2e for header match precedence and unit for grace_quota TTL.

sam: I'll add metrics to the ingestion pipeline and a dashboard prototype under Console -> Routing -> Fallbacks. Will include per-tenant histogram and alerts if grace_quota usage > 5% of total requests for >10m.

lee: Thanks — please ping here when PR and dashboard links are up. Also if anyone sees tenant-acme still spiking tag me. :thumbsup:
